result.title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning with State-Dependent Foresight for Human Decision-Making
result.summary: Computational modeling of behavior represents individuals with a model fitted to their observed behavior and characterizes them through its parameters. Naturalistic tasks incorporate the complexity of real environments and yield high-dimensional behavioral trajectories. Inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) infers the latent reward function underlying these trajectories. Standard IRL, however, assumes effectively infinite-horizon planning, whereas human foresight is both bounded and state-dependent. Here we introduce SC-AIRL (State-Conditional Adversarial IRL), which builds these two cognitive properties into the planner. Per-depth policies share one reward but differ in how far ahead they sum it explicitly. A state-conditional router mixes them according to the current state. Across held-out episodes in pedestrian crossing and highway overtaking tasks, SC-AIRL improves imitation over Standard AIRL, raising top-1 accuracy from 0.549 to 0.647 and from 0.629 to 0.718, respectively, while more closely reproducing participant behavior in rollouts. Inferred planning depth correlates with self-reported anxiety and motor impulsivity. SC-AIRL thus reproduces human behavior more closely than Standard AIRL while providing an interpretable, model-derived measure of state-dependent foresight.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SC-AIRL（状态条件对抗逆强化学习），把人类有限且随状态变化的规划前瞻深度写进规划器：多个不同显式求和深度的策略共享同一奖励，再由状态条件路由器按当前状态混合，在行人过街与高速超车任务上提升模仿精度，并将推断出的规划深度与焦虑、冲动性自评关联。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按共享奖励训练不同深度策略、由状态路由器决定实际前瞻长度」的机制，可能为 LVR 中随推理状态动态调整 latent 步数与停止决策提供可核查的结构线索，但原文既无视觉输入也未涉及语言模型推理。
